name: Göbekli Tepe
why: Carved T-shaped limestone pillars in large round enclosures, raised by communities who had not yet adopted farming.

name: Karahan Tepe
why: Sister site to Göbekli Tepe with rock-cut chambers, T-pillars and striking human and animal sculpture.

name: Nevalı Çori
why: Early village whose cult building with T-pillars first revealed the Taş Tepeler tradition; now beneath a reservoir.

name: Sayburç
why: Neolithic communal building with a carved wall relief of people and wild animals, among the oldest known narrative scenes.

name: Çakmaktepe
why: Taş Tepeler site with round rock-cut buildings that its excavators consider slightly older than Göbekli Tepe.

name: Çatalhöyük
why: Dense Neolithic town of mud-brick houses entered from the roof, with wall paintings and burials under the floors.

name: Aşıklı Höyük
why: One of the earliest villages in central Anatolia, documenting the shift to sheep and goat herding over a thousand years.

name: Boncuklu Tarla
why: Long-lived early settlement with communal buildings and thousands of beads, spanning the transition to village life.

name: Hallan Çemi
why: Very early sedentary hunter-gatherer village with round public buildings and decorated stone bowls.

name: Körtik Tepe
why: Early round-house village on the Tigris with rich burials and finely engraved stone vessels.

name: Çayönü
why: Neolithic village with a changing sequence of house plans, special buildings and very early copper working.

name: Tell Qaramel
why: Early settlement with a series of round stone towers, the oldest of which predate the tower at Jericho.

name: Jerf el Ahmar
why: Euphrates village with sunken communal buildings and engraved plaques; flooded by a dam after excavation.

name: Tell Abu Hureyra
why: Long-occupied village with some of the earliest evidence for cereal cultivation; now under Lake Assad.

name: Jericho (Tell es-Sultan)
why: Mound with a stone wall and tower built around 8300 BCE, among the earliest known large communal works.

name: 'Ain Ghazal
period: Pre-Pottery Neolithic B to Pottery Neolithic
why: Very large Neolithic village famous for its lime-plaster human statues, among the oldest large statues known.

name: Atlit Yam
why: Submerged Neolithic village off the Carmel coast with wells and a semicircle of standing stones.

name: Ohalo II
why: Waterlogged fisher-hunter camp preserving brush huts and thousands of plant remains from about 23,000 years ago.

name: Rujm el-Hiri
why: Concentric basalt stone rings around a central cairn; its date and purpose are still debated.

name: Khirokitia
why: Walled Neolithic village of round stone houses, one of the best preserved in the eastern Mediterranean.

name: Baalbek – Temple of Jupiter
why: Roman temple platform containing three roughly 800-tonne limestone blocks, among the largest ever moved.

name: Derinkuyu underground city
why: Multi-level underground town cut into soft tuff, able to shelter thousands; when digging began is uncertain.

name: Mount Nemrut
why: Mountain-top royal tumulus flanked by colossal seated statues whose heads now lie on the terraces.

name: Hattusa
why: Hittite capital with massive stone walls, sculpted gates and thousands of cuneiform tablets.

name: Troy
why: Layered citadel mound occupied for 3,500 years and tied to the Trojan War tradition.

name: Petra
why: Nabataean capital with monumental tomb facades cut into sandstone cliffs and an elaborate water system.

name: Hegra (Mada'in Salih)
why: Over a hundred monumental Nabataean tombs carved into isolated sandstone outcrops.

name: Mustatils of north-west Arabia
why: Over a thousand long rectangular stone enclosures, apparently for animal offerings, across north-west Arabia.

name: Rajajil
why: Clusters of tall sandstone pillars set in rows near Sakaka; purpose unknown.

name: Rock Art in the Hail Region (Jubbah and Shuwaymis)
why: Thousands of engravings of people and animals around a former lake, recording a once greener Arabia.

name: Dilmun Burial Mounds
why: Thousands of burial mounds, once among the densest prehistoric cemeteries anywhere.

name: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
why: Bronze Age towers and rows of beehive tombs, a well-preserved third-millennium landscape.

name: Shahr-e Sukhteh
why: Large mud-brick Bronze Age city in the desert with finds including an early artificial eye.

name: Chogha Zanbil
why: One of the best-preserved ziggurats, built by an Elamite king as a new religious centre.

name: Persepolis
why: Ceremonial capital of the Persian empire on a great terrace with carved stairways.

name: Ur
why: Sumerian city with a restored ziggurat and a royal cemetery of extraordinary richness.

name: Uruk
why: Often called the first true city, where monumental temples and the earliest writing appeared.

name: Eridu
why: Mound with a sequence of temples rebuilt on one spot for millennia; Sumerians called it the first city.

name: Babylon
why: Mesopotamian capital of vast mud-brick walls, the Ishtar Gate and a ziggurat behind the Babel story.

name: Shanidar Cave
why: Cave with Neanderthal skeletons that started the debate about deliberate Neanderthal burial.

name: Mehrgarh
why: One of the earliest farming villages in South Asia, a forerunner of the Indus civilisation.

name: Mohenjo-daro
why: Planned Indus city of baked brick with street grids, covered drains and the Great Bath.

name: Harappa
why: The city that gave the Indus civilisation its name, with granary platforms and standardised brickwork.

name: Dholavira
why: Indus city in the Rann of Kutch with stone architecture and a sophisticated system of reservoirs.

name: Lothal
why: Indus town with a large brick basin widely interpreted as a dockyard.

name: Rakhigarhi
why: Among the largest Indus civilisation sites; claims of much earlier occupation remain debated.

name: Bhimbetka rock shelters
why: Hundreds of painted rock shelters with art spanning many millennia; the oldest paintings are hard to date.

name: Hire Benakal
why: Hilltop field of hundreds of dolmens, one of the largest megalithic cemeteries in South India.

name: Ellora Caves
why: Rock-cut temples including Kailasa, a whole multi-storey temple carved downward from a single outcrop.

name: Sigiriya
why: Fifth-century palace on a sheer rock column, with frescoes, a lion gateway and water gardens.

name: Buddhas of Bamiyan
why: Two colossal Buddhas carved into a cliff, destroyed in 2001; the niches and caves remain.

name: Arkaim
why: Circular fortified Bronze Age settlement on the steppe; astronomical and mystical claims about it are not supported.

name: Sintashta
why: Fortified settlement and cemetery with the earliest known spoke-wheeled chariots.

name: Shigir Idol (from the Shigir peat bog)
why: Tall carved larch figure from a Urals peat bog, the oldest known monumental wooden sculpture.

name: Kapova Cave
why: Southern Urals cave with Ice Age paintings of mammoths and horses, far east of the classic cave-art region.

name: Por-Bazhyn
why: Clay-walled complex on a lake island in Tuva, apparently barely used; its purpose is debated.

name: Arzhan
why: Royal kurgans in Tuva with spectacular gold, among the earliest Scythian-type burials.

name: Denisova Cave
why: Altai cave where a finger bone revealed the Denisovans, a previously unknown human group.

name: Yana Rhinoceros Horn Site
why: Camp far above the Arctic Circle showing people lived in the high Arctic over 30,000 years ago.

name: Whale Bone Alley
why: Rows of bowhead whale jaws and skulls set upright along an Arctic beach in Chukotka.

name: Gonur Depe
why: Large Bronze Age oasis centre with a palace, temples and elaborate burials in the Karakum desert.

name: Tamgaly
why: Gorge with thousands of petroglyphs including distinctive sun-headed figures.

name: Petroglyphic Complexes of the Mongolian Altai
why: Rock art showing the shift from hunting big game to herding and horse nomadism.

name: Uushgiin Övör deer stones
why: Group of carved deer stones with stylised flying stags, beside stone burial mounds.

name: West Caucasus dolmens – Volkonsky dolmen
why: Rock-cut example of the thousands of West Caucasus stone tombs with distinctive round porthole openings.

name: Zorats Karer (Carahunge)
why: Over 200 standing stones, many with drilled holes; observatory claims and very early dates are disputed.

name: Gobustan rock art
why: Thousands of engravings of people, boats and animals near the Caspian shore.

name: Sannai-Maruyama Site
why: Large long-lived Jōmon village with pit houses and a structure raised on six massive chestnut posts.

name: Ōyu Stone Circles
why: Two large rings of river stones with sundial-like settings, built by Jōmon hunter-gatherers.

name: Daisen Kofun
why: Keyhole-shaped moated mound nearly 500 m long, one of the largest tombs on Earth by area.

name: Ishibutai Kofun
why: Exposed burial chamber of about thirty granite boulders, the largest megalithic chamber in Japan.

name: Masuda-no-iwafune
why: Carved granite block of about 800 tonnes on a hillside in Asuka; its purpose is unknown.

name: Yonaguni Monument
why: Underwater sandstone terraces that most geologists regard as natural jointing; claims of a sunken city lack evidence.

name: Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa Dolmen Sites
why: Hundreds of dolmens in three clusters, part of the densest concentration of dolmens in the world.

name: Bangudae Petroglyphs
why: Riverside rock panel with some of the earliest known depictions of whale hunting.

name: Liangzhu Ancient City
why: Walled Neolithic city with a palace platform, fine jades and a large system of dams.

name: Shimao
why: Vast stone-walled city with a stepped platform and carved stone faces on the Loess Plateau.

name: Taosi
why: Walled Neolithic town with elite tombs and a structure interpreted as a solar observatory.

name: Yinxu
why: Last Shang capital, source of the oracle bones bearing the earliest Chinese writing.

name: Sanxingdui
why: Walled Bronze Age site whose pits held giant bronze masks and trees unlike anything else in China.

name: Niuheliang
why: Neolithic ritual complex of stone cairns, altars and a temple with a life-sized clay face.

name: Jiahu
why: Early village with playable bone flutes and very early evidence of a fermented drink.

name: Xianren Cave
why: Cave that yielded pottery about 20,000 years old, the oldest known anywhere.

name: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor
why: Vast tomb complex guarded by the Terracotta Army; the central mound remains unopened.

name: Xiaohe Cemetery
why: Desert cemetery with boat-shaped coffins and exceptionally preserved mummies marked by tall wooden posts.

name: Longyou Caves
why: Large hand-cut sandstone caverns found in 1992, with no known historical record of their making.

name: Plain of Jars
why: Thousands of large stone jars across upland Laos, linked to burial; when they were first set up is debated.

name: Gunung Padang
why: Hilltop terraces of natural columnar basalt; claims of an Ice Age pyramid beneath were published and then retracted.

name: Bada Valley
why: Valley with large carved stone figures and stone vats whose makers and date are poorly known.

name: Borobudur
why: Huge stepped Buddhist monument covered in narrative reliefs and crowned with perforated stupas.

name: Maros-Pangkep cave art
why: Sulawesi caves with hand stencils and animal scenes, among the oldest dated figurative art.

name: Lubang Jeriji Saléh
why: Borneo cave with a painted wild bovid at least 40,000 years old.

name: Angkor Wat
why: Enormous moated temple-mountain, the largest religious monument in the world.

name: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
period: Uncertain: late prehistoric or early colonial
why: Mountain-side rice terraces; a traditional 2,000-year age is disputed by excavations suggesting about 400 years.

name: Beinan site
why: Large Neolithic village and slate-coffin cemetery with tall standing slate pillars.

name: Nan Madol
why: Ceremonial centre of nearly a hundred artificial islets walled with stacked basalt columns on a reef.

name: Leluh
why: Walled royal city of basalt and coral on a reef flat, with truncated pyramid tombs.

name: Rano Raraku
why: Volcanic crater quarry where almost all the moai were carved; hundreds remain on its slopes.

name: Ahu Tongariki
why: Largest ceremonial platform on Rapa Nui, with fifteen re-erected moai.

name: Orongo
why: Clifftop ceremonial village of stone houses and birdman petroglyphs.

name: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
why: Trilithon of three coral limestone slabs, each weighing tens of tonnes.

name: Taputapuatea marae
why: Large stone temple complex regarded as a ceremonial centre of eastern Polynesia.

name: Pulemelei mound
why: Largest ancient structure in Polynesia, a stone platform mound in the forest of Savaiʻi.

name: House of Taga
why: Tallest erected latte stones in the Marianas, capped pillars that once carried a house.

name: Badrulchau
why: Rows of large basalt monoliths, some with carved faces, on a terraced hillside.

name: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
why: Highland wetland with ditches and mounds showing farming arose independently in New Guinea.

name: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
why: Home, death place and mass burial of a chief whose story was kept in oral tradition.

name: Teouma
why: Oldest known cemetery in the Pacific islands, with decorated Lapita burial pots.

name: Piʻilanihale Heiau
why: Massive lava-rock temple platform, the largest heiau in Hawaiʻi.

name: Wairau Bar
why: One of the earliest settlements in New Zealand, with burials of first-generation Polynesian arrivals.

name: Budj Bim
why: Channels, weirs and ponds cut in lava flow for trapping eels, one of the oldest aquaculture systems.

name: Brewarrina Aboriginal Fish Traps
why: Complex of dry-stone weirs and pens in the Barwon River; their age is unknown.

name: Wurdi Youang
why: Egg-shaped Aboriginal stone arrangement; a proposed solstice alignment and great age are not established.

name: Murujuga
why: Possibly the densest concentration of rock engravings in the world, including extinct animals.

name: Madjedbebe
why: Rock shelter with the earliest widely cited evidence of people in Australia, about 65,000 years ago.

name: Lake Mungo (Mungo Lady and Mungo Man)
why: Burials about 42,000 years old, including one of the earliest known cremations.

name: Nawarla Gabarnmang
why: Rock shelter whose pillared ceiling is densely painted, with one of the oldest dated paintings in Australia.

name: Stonehenge
why: Ring of dressed sarsens and Welsh bluestones aligned on the solstices, rebuilt over 1,500 years.

name: Avebury
why: Largest stone circle in the world, set inside a massive ditch and bank.

name: Silbury Hill
why: Largest prehistoric artificial mound in Europe; no burial has been found and its purpose is unknown.

name: West Kennet Long Barrow
why: Long chambered tomb with a sarsen facade, used for communal burial.

name: Durrington Walls
why: Huge henge and settlement thought to have housed the builders of Stonehenge.

name: Maiden Castle, Dorset
why: One of the largest Iron Age hillforts in Europe, with huge multiple ramparts.

name: Uffington White Horse
period: Late Bronze Age to Iron Age
why: Stylised horse cut into chalk hillside, kept visible by regular scouring for some 3,000 years.

name: Cerne Abbas Giant
why: Chalk hill figure of a club-wielding man, dated to the early medieval period in 2021.

name: Star Carr
why: Lakeside Mesolithic site with red deer antler headdresses and early timber platforms.

name: Grime's Graves
why: Hundreds of Neolithic flint mine shafts dug with antler picks.

name: Seahenge
why: Timber circle around an upturned oak stump, dated by tree rings to 2049 BCE.

name: Castlerigg stone circle
why: Early stone circle in a dramatic ring of Lake District fells.

name: Rollright Stones
why: Stone circle, portal dolmen and standing stone built in different periods.

name: Wayland's Smithy
why: Chambered long barrow on the Ridgeway, closely dated to within a few decades.

name: Bryn Celli Ddu
why: Passage tomb on Anglesey aligned on the midsummer sunrise.

name: Skara Brae
why: Stone-built Neolithic village with intact stone furniture, preserved under sand.

name: Ness of Brodgar
why: Walled complex of large Neolithic stone buildings between two stone circles in Orkney.

name: Ring of Brodgar
why: Large stone circle in a rock-cut ditch on an isthmus between two lochs.

name: Standing Stones of Stenness
why: Possibly the oldest henge in the British Isles, with thin slabs up to six metres tall.

name: Maeshowe
why: Finely built chambered tomb lit by the midwinter sunset, later carved with Norse runes.

name: Knap of Howar
why: Two stone farmhouses, among the oldest standing houses in northern Europe.

name: Callanish Stones
why: Cross-shaped setting of tall gneiss stones around a small circle on Lewis.

name: Balnuaran of Clava (Clava cairns)
why: Ring cairns and passage graves surrounded by stone circles near Inverness.

name: Mousa Broch
why: Best-preserved broch, a thirteen-metre drystone tower with a stair inside its double wall.

name: Warren Field
why: Mesolithic pit alignment interpreted by some researchers as a lunar calendar.

name: Newgrange
why: Great passage tomb whose roof-box lets the midwinter sunrise reach the chamber.

name: Knowth
why: Passage tomb complex holding the largest collection of megalithic art in Europe.

name: Loughcrew
why: Hilltop passage tomb cemetery with carved stones lit by the equinox sunrise.

name: Carrowmore
why: One of the largest and oldest clusters of megalithic tombs in Ireland.

name: Poulnabrone dolmen
why: Portal tomb on limestone pavement that held the remains of over thirty people.

name: Céide Fields
why: Stone-walled field system buried under blanket bog; a Neolithic date is widely but not universally accepted.

name: Hill of Tara
why: Ridge of tombs and enclosures remembered as the seat of the high kings.

name: Navan Fort
why: Huge timber structure built about 95 BCE, then filled with stones, burned and buried.

name: Dún Aonghasa
why: Drystone fort of concentric walls on the edge of a hundred-metre Atlantic cliff.

name: Carnac stones
why: Thousands of standing stones in long parallel rows, the largest such alignments known.

name: Barnenez
why: Long stepped cairn with eleven chambers, one of the oldest large stone buildings in Europe.

name: Grand Menhir Brisé (Locmariaquer megaliths)
why: Includes the broken Grand Menhir, once over twenty metres tall and about 300 tonnes.

name: Gavrinis
why: Passage tomb on a small island whose slabs are covered in dense carved patterns.

name: Tumulus of Bougon
why: Group of early Atlantic burial mounds, among the oldest monumental tombs in France.

name: Filitosa
why: Corsican site with granite statue-menhirs carved with faces and weapons.

name: Lascaux
why: Cave with vivid paintings of aurochs, horses and deer about 17,000 years old.

name: Chauvet Cave
why: Among the oldest known cave paintings, with skilled shaded images of lions and rhinos.

name: Bruniquel Cave
why: Rings of broken stalagmites built deep underground by Neanderthals about 176,000 years ago.

name: Vallée des Merveilles
why: High alpine valley with tens of thousands of engravings of horned cattle, weapons and figures.

name: Neolithic flint mines of Spiennes
why: Among the largest and earliest flint mining complexes in Europe.

name: Antequera Dolmens Site
why: Three great tombs including Menga, roofed with slabs of up to 150 tonnes.

name: Los Millares
why: Copper Age town with lines of bastioned walls, outlying forts and a tholos cemetery.

name: Dolmen de La Pastora (Valencina Copper Age site)
why: Very large Copper Age site with great tholos tombs and rich ivory and crystal grave goods.

name: Motilla del Azuer
why: Concentric-walled Bronze Age fort around the oldest known well in Iberia.

name: Naveta d'Es Tudons
why: Boat-shaped collective tomb of large dry-laid blocks on Menorca.

name: Cave of Altamira
why: Cave whose painted bison ceiling was the first Ice Age art to be recognised.

name: Cave of El Castillo
why: Cave art including a red disc dated to at least 40,800 years ago.

name: Almendres Cromlech
why: Large oval of rounded standing stones, begun earlier than most stone circles further north.

name: Anta Grande do Zambujeiro
why: One of the tallest dolmens in Europe, with uprights about six metres high.

name: Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley
why: Largest known group of open-air Ice Age engravings, saved from a planned dam.

name: Ġgantija
why: Two temples on Gozo with walls of huge limestone blocks, among the oldest free-standing stone buildings.

name: Ħaġar Qim
why: Clifftop temple including a single block weighing about twenty tonnes.

name: Mnajdra
why: Three joined temples, one aligned so the equinox sunrise shines through its doorway.

name: Tarxien Temples
why: Temple complex rich in spiral and animal reliefs, with the base of a colossal statue.

name: Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum
why: Underground complex carved on three levels imitating temple architecture, used for thousands of burials.

name: Xagħra Stone Circle
why: Underground burial caves ringed by megaliths, holding the remains of hundreds of people.

name: Misraħ Għar il-Kbir cart ruts
why: Dense network of parallel grooves worn into bare limestone; their date and exact cause are unresolved.

name: Su Nuraxi (Barumini)
why: Best-known nuraghe, a basalt tower with bastions and a surrounding village.

name: Monte d'Accoddi
why: Stepped platform with a ramp, unique in the prehistoric Mediterranean.

name: Giants' grave of Coddu Vecchiu
why: Collective tomb fronted by a tall carved stele and a curved stone facade.

name: Necropolis of Pantalica
why: Thousands of chamber tombs honeycombing limestone gorges in Sicily.

name: Rock Drawings in Valcamonica
why: One of the largest collections of prehistoric petroglyphs, made over some 8,000 years.

name: Saint-Martin-de-Corléans megalithic area
why: Ritual area in Aosta with ploughed furrows, post rows and finely carved human-shaped stelae.

name: Sassi di Matera
why: Districts of cave dwellings cut into a ravine and lived in for millennia.

name: Banditaccia necropolis (Cerveteri)
why: Etruscan city of the dead with streets of rock-cut tumulus tombs modelled on houses.

name: Knossos
why: Largest Minoan palace, built on one of the oldest Neolithic settlements in Europe.

name: Akrotiri
why: Bronze Age town buried by the Thera eruption, with multi-storey houses and wall paintings.

name: Mycenae
why: Citadel with cyclopean walls, the Lion Gate and great corbelled tholos tombs.

name: Sesklo
why: One of the earliest farming villages in Europe, with stone-founded houses.

name: Dimini
why: Neolithic hilltop settlement ringed by concentric stone walls.

name: Franchthi Cave
why: Cave occupied over some 35,000 years, with early evidence of seafaring for obsidian.

name: Dispilio
why: Neolithic lakeside village, find spot of a wooden tablet with debated incised signs.

name: Keros
why: Island sanctuary where broken marble figurines were deposited, with a terraced settlement on an adjoining islet.

name: Lepenski Vir
why: Danube fishing village with trapezoidal houses and fish-like sandstone sculptures.

name: Vinča-Belo Brdo
why: Large tell and type site of a culture with early copper working and incised symbols.

name: Varna Necropolis
why: Cemetery containing the oldest known large hoard of worked gold.

name: Solnitsata
why: Fortified salt-production centre sometimes described as the oldest town in Europe.

name: Kokino
why: Bronze Age hilltop site with offerings; its promotion as an ancient observatory is disputed.

name: Bosnian "pyramids" (Visočica hill)
why: Natural flatiron hills promoted since 2005 as giant pyramids; geologists and archaeologists reject the claim.

name: Sarmizegetusa Regia
why: Dacian mountain capital with terraces, sanctuaries and a circular andesite setting.

name: Talianki
why: Largest of the Trypillia mega-sites, with thousands of houses arranged in concentric rings.

name: Nebelivka
why: Trypillia mega-site with a very large public building, among the biggest settlements of its time.

name: Kamyana Mohyla
why: Sandstone mound with engraved grottoes; some far-reaching readings of its signs are not accepted.

name: Sungir
why: Ice Age burials dressed in thousands of mammoth-ivory beads.

name: Bolshoi Zayatsky labyrinths
why: Group of turf-and-boulder labyrinths on a White Sea island; their age is disputed.

name: Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea
why: Thousands of carvings of birds, boats and hunters on lakeshore and river rocks.

name: Dolní Věstonice
why: Mammoth-hunter camp with the oldest known fired ceramic figures and a triple burial.

name: Goseck circle
why: Ring ditch and palisades with gates aligned on the winter solstice.

name: Pömmelte ring sanctuary
period: Bell Beaker to Early Bronze Age
why: Timber ring sanctuary with offerings and burials, comparable in plan to British henges.

name: Heuneburg
why: Celtic hillfort with a Mediterranean-style mud-brick wall, possibly the Pyrene of Herodotus.

name: Hohle Fels
why: Cave that produced the oldest known figurine of a human and early bone flutes.

name: Externsteine
why: Sandstone pillars with medieval chambers and a relief; claims of a pagan sanctuary lack archaeological support.

name: Hallstatt salt mines and cemetery
why: Prehistoric salt mines and a rich cemetery that named an entire Iron Age culture.

name: Biskupin
why: Waterlogged fortified timber settlement dated by tree rings to 738 BCE.

name: Ale's Stones
why: Ship-shaped setting of 59 boulders on a sea cliff; dating has been disputed.

name: The King's Grave
why: Huge cairn with a cist of slabs carved with ships, horses and processions.

name: Rock Carvings in Tanum
why: Thousands of carvings of ships, warriors and ploughing scenes.

name: Rock art of Alta
why: Thousands of carvings of reindeer, boats and hunters inside the Arctic Circle.

name: Kastelli Giant's Church
why: Large rectangular stone enclosure built by hunter-gatherers; its purpose is unknown.

name: Giza pyramid complex
why: Three great pyramids and the Sphinx; the Great Pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for about 3,800 years.

name: Saqqara
why: Necropolis of Memphis with Djoser's Step Pyramid, the first large building made entirely of cut stone.

name: Dahshur
why: Site of the Bent and Red Pyramids, where builders worked out the true smooth-sided pyramid.

name: Meidum
why: Partly collapsed pyramid marking the change from stepped to smooth-sided design.

name: Abydos
why: Burial place of the first pharaohs, with the temple of Seti I and the unusual sunken Osireion.

name: Karnak
why: Vast temple precinct built over two millennia, with a hall of 134 giant columns.

name: Abu Simbel
why: Two rock-cut temples with colossal statues of Ramesses II, moved in the 1960s to escape Lake Nasser.

name: Valley of the Kings
why: Desert valley of rock-cut royal tombs, including that of Tutankhamun.

name: Hierakonpolis (Nekhen)
why: Largest Predynastic town in Egypt, with an early temple, painted tomb and elite cemetery.

name: Nabta Playa
why: Seasonal lake basin with a small stone circle, megalith alignments and cattle burials made by desert herders.

name: Serapeum of Saqqara
why: Underground galleries holding granite sarcophagi of sixty tonnes or more for the sacred Apis bulls.

name: Unfinished obelisk
why: Abandoned obelisk still in the Aswan granite quarry; it would have weighed over 1,000 tonnes.

name: Amarna
why: Capital built from nothing by Akhenaten and abandoned within about twenty years.

name: Cave of Swimmers
why: Painted shelter in the deep Sahara with small figures that appear to swim.

name: Cave of Beasts
why: Remote desert shelter with thousands of painted figures, including headless beasts.

name: Qurta
why: Nile-side engravings of wild cattle at least 15,000 years old, the oldest dated rock art in North Africa.

name: Jebel Sahaba
why: Cemetery where many skeletons show weapon injuries, among the earliest evidence of repeated group violence.

name: Meroë
why: Kushite royal city with fields of steep-sided pyramids.

name: Kerma
why: Capital of an early Nubian kingdom with a massive mud-brick temple and huge royal tumuli.

name: Jebel Barkal
why: Sacred flat-topped mountain with temples and pyramids at the religious heart of Kush.

name: Aksum stelae field
why: Carved granite stelae up to 33 metres long, among the largest single stones ever erected.

name: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
why: Eleven churches cut downward into solid rock and linked by trenches and tunnels.

name: Tiya
why: Field of carved stelae marked with swords and symbols, standing over graves.

name: Temple of Yeha
why: Tall temple of finely fitted stone, the oldest standing building in Ethiopia.

name: Laas Geel
why: Rock shelters with vivid polychrome paintings of decorated cattle and herders.

name: Namoratunga
why: Basalt pillar site near Lake Turkana; an early claim that it is an astronomical observatory is disputed.

name: Thimlich Ohinga
why: Dry-stone walled enclosures built without mortar near Lake Victoria.

name: Engaruka
why: Abandoned farming settlement with an extensive stone-lined irrigation system.

name: Kilwa Kisiwani
why: Swahili island port with a great coral-stone mosque and palace.

name: Kondoa Rock-Art Sites
why: Many painted shelters on the Rift escarpment; the oldest paintings are hard to date.

name: Bigo bya Mugenyi
why: Kilometres of ditches and banks enclosing a large area of grassland.

name: Kalambo Falls
why: Waterlogged site with shaped, interlocking logs about 476,000 years old, the earliest known wooden structure.

name: Great Zimbabwe
why: Largest ancient stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa, with mortarless granite walls up to eleven metres high.

name: Khami
why: Successor capital to Great Zimbabwe with decorated stone-faced terraces.

name: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
why: Hilltop capital of an early southern African state, with gold-rich elite burials.

name: Blombos Cave
why: Cave with engraved ochre and shell beads, among the earliest evidence of symbolic behaviour.

name: Blaauboschkraal stone ruins
why: Stone-walled Bokoni homesteads and cattle roads; fringe writers recast such ruins as the far older 'Adam's Calendar', which archaeologists reject.

name: Tsodilo
why: Kalahari hills with thousands of rock paintings and evidence of very long human use.

name: Twyfelfontein
why: One of the largest concentrations of rock engravings in Africa.

name: Apollo 11 Cave
why: Cave that yielded painted stone slabs about 27,000 years old, among the oldest figurative art in Africa.

name: Senegambian stone circles
why: Over a thousand stone circles of cut laterite pillars with associated burials.

name: Dhar Tichitt
why: Stone-walled villages along a desert escarpment, among the oldest settlements of their kind in West Africa.

name: Djenné-Djenno
why: One of the oldest urbanised centres south of the Sahara, grown without outside rule.

name: Sungbo's Eredo
why: Rampart and ditch about 160 kilometres long, hidden in rainforest.

name: Walls of Benin
why: Enormous network of earthen banks and ditches around Benin City and its villages.

name: Ikom monoliths
why: Groups of carved basalt stones with faces and symbols; their age is poorly known.

name: Igbo-Ukwu
why: Burial and shrine with intricate lost-wax bronzes made using local techniques.

name: Ruins of Loropéni
why: High laterite stone walls linked to the trans-Saharan gold trade.

name: Diy-Gid-Biy
why: Dry-stone platforms and terraces in the Mandara Mountains.

name: Tassili n'Ajjer
why: Sandstone plateau with thousands of paintings recording the Sahara's change from savanna to desert.

name: Tadrart Acacus
why: Desert massif with paintings and engravings of wild animals, cattle, horses and camels.

name: Dabous Giraffes
why: Two life-sized giraffes engraved on a sandstone outcrop.

name: Gobero
why: Largest Stone Age cemetery in the Sahara, beside a former lake.

name: Msoura
why: Ring of 167 standing stones around a large tumulus, one stone over five metres tall.

name: Madghacen
why: Round stepped royal mausoleum of the Numidian kings.

name: Pyramids of Güímar
why: Stepped lava-stone terraces; excavation dates them to the nineteenth century, against claims of ancient origin.

name: Poverty Point
why: Concentric earthen ridges and a huge mound built by hunter-gatherers.

name: Watson Brake
why: Ring of eleven mounds built by hunter-gatherers, older than the Egyptian pyramids.

name: Cahokia
why: Largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, centred on a huge flat-topped earthen mound.

name: Serpent Mound
why: Earthen effigy of a snake about 400 metres long; researchers disagree on which culture built it.

name: Newark Earthworks
why: Precise geometric enclosures including an octagon aligned to the 18.6-year lunar cycle.

name: Hopewell Culture National Historical Park
why: Mound groups and enclosures with finely crafted objects of materials from across the continent.

name: Fort Ancient
why: Hilltop enclosed by about five kilometres of earthen walls.

name: Grave Creek Mound
why: One of the largest conical burial mounds in the United States.

name: Moundville Archaeological Site
why: Planned town of platform mounds around a plaza.

name: Etowah Indian Mounds
why: Platform mounds and elite burials with embossed copper plates.

name: Spiro Mounds
why: Ceremonial centre whose main mound held an exceptional cache of art in shell, copper and textile.

name: Pinson Mounds
why: Large Woodland mound complex including one of the tallest mounds in the United States.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
why: Over 200 mounds, many shaped like bears and birds.

name: Aztalan State Park
why: Northern Mississippian outpost with platform mounds and a stockade.

name: Miami Circle
why: Ring of holes cut into limestone bedrock in central Miami, the footing of a Tequesta structure.

name: Windover Archeological Site
why: Pond cemetery whose peat preserved woven textiles and brain tissue for about 7,000 years.

name: Pueblo Bonito
why: Largest great house of Chaco Canyon, a planned multi-storey building of about 800 rooms.

name: Cliff Palace
why: Largest cliff dwelling in North America, built under a sandstone overhang.

name: Taos Pueblo
why: Multi-storey adobe village inhabited continuously for many centuries.

name: Horseshoe Canyon (Great Gallery)
why: Rock art panel of life-sized ghostly figures; its age is debated.

name: Bighorn Medicine Wheel
why: Spoked stone circle high in the Bighorn Mountains, still used ceremonially.

name: Blythe Intaglios
why: Giant human and animal figures scraped into desert pavement near the Colorado River.

name: Meadowcroft Rockshelter
why: Rock shelter with a long sequence; its oldest pre-Clovis layers were long disputed.

name: Paisley Caves
why: Caves where preserved human coprolites dated occupation to about 14,300 years ago.

name: Blackwater Draw
why: Type site of the Clovis culture, where fluted points lay among mammoth bones.

name: Cerutti Mastodon site
why: Broken mastodon bones claimed to show humans in America 130,000 years ago; most archaeologists are unconvinced.

name: America's Stonehenge
why: Stone chambers and walls promoted as ancient and pre-Columbian; most archaeologists attribute them to colonial-era farmers.

name: Bimini Road
why: Underwater line of limestone blocks that geologists identify as naturally jointed beachrock.

name: Newport Tower
why: Stone tower often claimed to be Norse or older; excavation and mortar dating point to a seventeenth-century windmill.

name: L'Anse aux Meadows
why: Only confirmed Norse site in the Americas, dated by tree rings to 1021 CE.

name: Bluefish Caves
why: Yukon caves with cut-marked bones claimed as 24,000 years old; the evidence is debated.

name: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
why: Cliff used for nearly 6,000 years to drive bison herds, with deep bone beds below.

name: Majorville Cairn and Medicine Wheel site
why: Central cairn with radiating spokes, added to for about 5,000 years.

name: Writing-on-Stone / Áísínai'pi
why: Largest concentration of rock art on the North American plains.

name: Petroglyphs Provincial Park
why: Largest known concentration of Indigenous rock carvings in Canada.

name: Ipiutak site
why: Large Arctic settlement and cemetery with elaborate carved ivory.

name: Qilakitsoq
why: Rock-shelter graves that preserved eight naturally mummified Inuit and their clothing.

name: Hvalsey Church
why: Best-preserved Norse ruin in Greenland, site of the last written record of the colony.

name: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán
why: Earliest major Olmec centre, source of ten colossal basalt heads.

name: La Venta
why: Olmec centre with an early earthen pyramid, buried mosaic pavements and colossal heads.

name: Aguada Fénix
why: Artificial platform 1.4 km long found by lidar, the largest and oldest known Maya monument.

name: Paso de la Amada
why: Early village with the oldest known Mesoamerican ballcourt.

name: Guilá Naquitz Cave
why: Small cave with the earliest known domesticated squash and very early maize cobs.

name: Chalcatzingo
why: Highland site with Olmec-style reliefs carved on cliff faces.

name: Cuicuilco
why: Large circular stepped pyramid partly buried by a lava flow.

name: Teotihuacan
why: Planned city of over 100,000 people with the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

name: Great Pyramid of Cholula
why: Largest pyramid by volume in the world, now resembling a hill topped by a church.

name: Monte Albán
why: Zapotec capital on a levelled mountain top, with carved slabs and an arrow-shaped building.

name: Mitla
why: Palaces covered in geometric stone mosaic fretwork.

name: El Tajín
why: City with the Pyramid of the Niches and many ballcourts.

name: Guachimontones
why: Circular stepped pyramids ringed by platforms, a layout unique to western Mexico.

name: Paquimé (Casas Grandes)
why: Adobe city blending Puebloan and Mesoamerican traditions.

name: Rock Paintings of Sierra de San Francisco
why: Larger-than-life painted figures on high shelter walls; the oldest dates are debated.

name: Templo Mayor
why: Main temple of Tenochtitlan, rebuilt seven times and rediscovered under Mexico City.

name: Tikal
why: Major Maya city with steep temple pyramids rising above the forest.

name: El Mirador
why: Huge Preclassic Maya city whose La Danta complex is among the largest ancient structures by volume.

name: San Bartolo
why: Site with finely painted murals and some of the earliest Maya writing.

name: Takalik Abaj
why: Site with both Olmec-style and early Maya sculpture.

name: Quiriguá
why: Maya site with the tallest carved stelae in the Americas.

name: Calakmul
why: Maya superpower deep in the forest, with one of the largest Maya pyramids.

name: Palenque
why: Maya city of refined architecture and the tomb of Pakal.

name: Chichen Itza
why: Maya city where the main pyramid casts a serpent-like shadow at the equinoxes.

name: Copán
why: Maya city with a hieroglyphic stairway bearing the longest known Maya text.

name: Caracol
why: Very large Maya city mapped by lidar, with extensive terraces and causeways.

name: Joya de Cerén
why: Farming village buried by volcanic ash, preserving everyday life in detail.

name: Stone spheres of Costa Rica
why: Hundreds of near-perfect stone balls up to two metres across.

name: Guayabo de Turrialba
why: Forest town with stone mounds, paved causeways and working aqueducts.

name: Caguana Ceremonial Ball Courts Site
why: Taíno plazas edged with standing stones bearing petroglyphs.

name: Caral
why: Large centre with pyramids and sunken circular plazas, among the oldest cities in the Americas.

name: Aspero
why: Coastal fishing town with early platform mounds, linked to Caral.

name: Bandurria
why: Early coastal monumental site with mounds and a sunken circular plaza.

name: El Paraíso
why: Large stone complex near Lima built before pottery was in use.

name: Sechin Bajo
why: Site with a circular sunken plaza dated to about 3500 BCE, the oldest known monumental building in the Americas.

name: Cerro Sechín
why: Temple wall of carved slabs showing warriors and dismembered bodies.

name: Chankillo
why: Row of thirteen towers on a ridge marking sunrise through the year, a complete solar calendar.

name: Kotosh
why: Highland temple site known for its clay relief of crossed hands.

name: Huaca Prieta
why: Coastal mound with very early occupation and some of the oldest cotton textiles and indigo dye.

name: Ventarron
why: Temple with the oldest known wall paintings in the Americas, damaged by fire in 2017.

name: Chavín de Huántar
why: Highland temple with underground galleries, stone drains and the carved Lanzón monolith.

name: Kuntur Wasi
why: Hilltop temple with stone sculpture and some of the earliest goldwork in the Andes.

name: Nazca Lines
why: Hundreds of lines, shapes and animal figures made by clearing desert stones.

name: Paracas Candelabra
why: Trident-like figure about 180 metres tall cut into a coastal slope.

name: Cahuachi
why: Adobe ceremonial centre of the Nazca, overlooking the lines.

name: Huaca de la Luna
why: Moche adobe temple with layered polychrome murals.

name: Sipán
why: Unlooted Moche royal tombs with spectacular gold and silver.

name: Chan Chan
why: Largest adobe city in the Americas, with walled royal compounds.

name: Pachacamac
why: Coastal oracle and pilgrimage centre used for over a thousand years.

name: Kuélap
why: Mountain-top settlement behind stone walls up to nineteen metres high.

name: Wari
why: Capital of the Wari, one of the earliest Andean empires.

name: Machu Picchu
why: Inca royal estate on a mountain ridge, with fine fitted masonry.

name: Sacsayhuamán
why: Zigzag walls of precisely fitted limestone blocks weighing up to about 100 tonnes.

name: Ollantaytambo – Temple of the Sun
why: Inca estate and unfinished temple with six huge fitted pink granite slabs.

name: Moray
why: Concentric circular terraces set in natural hollows, possibly for crop experiments.

name: Sillustani
why: Tall round stone burial towers on a lake peninsula.

name: Band of Holes
why: Band of thousands of pits along a ridge; storage or accounting has been proposed.

name: Toro Muerto
why: Desert valley with thousands of carved volcanic boulders.

name: Cumbe Mayo
why: Rock-cut canal with right-angle turns high in the Andes.

name: Marcahuasi
why: Plateau of granite formations eroded into shapes some read as sculptures; geologists regard them as natural.

name: Tiwanaku
why: High-altitude ceremonial city near Lake Titicaca; claims of extreme antiquity are not supported by radiocarbon dates.

name: Pumapunku
why: Platform complex with precisely cut andesite and sandstone blocks.

name: El Fuerte de Samaipata
why: Huge sandstone outcrop carved with channels, seats and niches.

name: Ingapirca
why: Largest Inca site in Ecuador, with an elliptical temple.

name: Real Alto
why: Early village with a plaza and ceremonial mounds, among the oldest in the Americas.

name: Santa Ana (La Florida)
why: Upper Amazon site with spiral architecture and the earliest evidence of cacao use.

name: Upano Valley sites
why: Lidar-mapped network of platforms, plazas and straight roads in the Amazon.

name: San Agustín Archaeological Park
why: Largest group of megalithic sculptures in South America, guarding tombs.

name: Tierradentro
why: Underground tombs reached by spiral stairs, with painted walls.

name: Ciudad Perdida
why: Terraced mountain town reached by over a thousand stone steps.

name: El Infiernito
why: Rows of stone columns interpreted as a solar calendar.

name: Chiribiquete rock art
why: Remote table mountains with tens of thousands of paintings; the oldest dates are debated.

name: Serra da Capivara National Park
why: Hundreds of painted shelters; claims of occupation before 30,000 years ago remain controversial.

name: Calçoene megalithic site
why: Circle of granite blocks in Amapá that appears to mark the winter solstice.

name: Kuhikugu
why: Cluster of large ditched settlements joined by roads in the Upper Xingu.

name: Ingá Stone
why: Long gneiss outcrop covered in deeply cut symbols of unknown age and meaning.

name: Monte Verde
why: Waterlogged camp about 14,500 years old that overturned the Clovis-first model.

name: Atacama Giant
why: Largest prehistoric human-like figure in the world, 119 metres long on a desert hillside.

name: Cueva de las Manos
why: Cave walls covered with hundreds of stencilled hands and hunting scenes.

name: Ruins of Quilmes
why: Large terraced pre-Columbian town that resisted the Inca and then the Spanish.

name: Acre geoglyphs
why: Hundreds of geometric ditched enclosures revealed by deforestation, showing large-scale earth-building in western Amazonia.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
why: Great stupa of Anuradhapura, built about 140 BCE by King Dutugemunu according to the Mahavamsa chronicle; restored in the twentieth century.

name: Abhayagiri Vihāra
why: Monastery and stupa at Anuradhapura that the chronicle says King Valagamba founded between 89 and 77 BCE; it grew into a centre of Buddhist learning with foreign scholars.

name: Jetavanaramaya
why: Brick stupa begun by King Mahasena, who reigned 273 to 301, and finished by his son; about 122 metres high when built, among the tallest structures of the ancient world.

name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
why: Sacred fig tree at Anuradhapura; Sri Lankan tradition says it grew from a cutting of the Bodh Gaya tree brought by the nun Sangamitta in 236 BCE.

name: Dambulla cave temple
why: Five caves under an overhanging rock holding 153 Buddha statues and extensive murals; King Valagamba is traditionally thought to have made them a temple in the first century BCE.

name: Sanchi
why: Hilltop Buddhist complex whose brick Great Stupa was commissioned by Ashoka in the third century BCE; four carved stone gateways were added in the first century BCE.

name: Konark Sun Temple
why: Temple to the sun god Surya built as a stone chariot with carved wheels and horses, attributed to King Narasingha Deva I about 1250; its main tower has fallen.

name: Chand Baori
why: Stepwell at Abhaneri about 30 metres deep, with flights of steps down thirteen storeys; dated on style to the eighth or ninth century.

name: Kallanai (Grand Anicut)
why: Stone dam across the Kaveri, attributed to the Chola king Karikala about 100 to 150 CE and remodelled by British engineers in the nineteenth century; still in use.

name: Shore Temple of Mahabalipuram
why: Granite temple complex on the Bay of Bengal shore, credited to Narasimhavarman II; one of the oldest structural, rather than rock-cut, stone temples of southern India.

name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
why: Shiva temple with a history from about the seventh century, enlarged under the Vijayanagara rulers; still a place of pilgrimage after the city was destroyed in 1565.

name: Vitthala Temple, Hampi
why: Ruined temple and market complex with a stone chariot shrine in its courtyard; builder and date are unclear, and most scholars place it in the early to mid sixteenth century.

name: Lumbini
why: Held by Buddhist tradition to be the Buddha's birthplace; Ashoka's inscribed pillar records his visit in the third century BCE. An older timber structure found beneath the shrine in 2013 is disputed.

name: Yungang Grottoes
why: Buddhist cave temples cut into a sandstone cliff near Datong in the fifth and early sixth centuries, with 53 major caves; work stopped in 525.

name: Longmen Grottoes
why: More than two thousand caves and niches of Buddhist sculpture cut into limestone cliffs on both banks of the Yi River, most of them Northern Wei or Tang.

name: Pagoda of Fogong Temple
why: Wooden pagoda of Ying County, 67 metres high, built in 1056 and enlarged in 1195; the oldest fully wooden pagoda still standing in China.

name: Dujiangyan
why: Irrigation and flood-control works on the Min River, built about 256 BCE; they divide and channel the river instead of damming it and are still in use.

name: Jiayu Pass
why: Fortress at the west end of the Ming Great Wall, built about 1372, through which merchants and envoys from Central and West Asia entered China.

name: Yumen Pass (Jade Gate)
why: Frontier post west of Dunhuang, first set up under Emperor Wu of Han soon after 121 BCE, where the Silk Road left Han territory for the Western Regions.

name: Cheomseongdae
why: Stone tower at Gyeongju built in the reign of Queen Seondeok, described as the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in Asia.

name: Colossal statue of Shapur I
why: Statue of the Sasanian king Shapur I, 6.7 metres tall, carved from a single stalagmite inside Shapur Cave near Bishapur; it lay fallen for centuries and was raised again in 1957.

name: Uçhisar Castle
why: Rock cone 60 metres high in Cappadocia, riddled with cut rooms and passages that served as dwellings and perhaps cloisters in Byzantine times.

name: Boa Island figures
why: Two carved stone figures in Caldragh graveyard, one of them two-faced; they are assumed to be Iron Age, but when and why they were made is unknown.
